purpose: Wire three already-implemented but currently disconnected/broken pieces of callisto's fixed-group version engine into the real command call paths: (1) make fixed-group siblings converge on a single shared group-aligned target version instead of each bumping independently from its own base, by adding a new Fixed-group convergence block to cascade.rs's solve_cascade — structurally mirroring the pre-existing Linked-group convergence block at lines 314-379 — that iterates input.groups.fixed.values(), computes one shared target via the existing fixed_group_target function, and assigns that target to every member of each Fixed group, participating in the same `while changed` fixpoint loop; (2) call the existing, fully-implemented pre_mutation_checks divergence/napi-drift detector from callisto-graph's real version-command orchestration path, before mutation, and actually consume its result (merge diagnostics, abort on divergence error); (3) add cross-group conflict detection to GroupTable::resolve so that two differently-spelled group members that resolve to the same PackageId across two different groups produce GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership instead of silently overwriting one group's claim with the other's.
scope: crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs (CascadeInput struct gains a `tags` field, including the seven pre-existing CascadeInput literals in cascade.rs's own #[cfg(test)] mod tests block, which must each be updated to supply it; solve_cascade gains a new Fixed-group convergence block added within the existing `while changed` fixpoint loop, positioned alongside the pre-existing Linked-group block at lines 314-379 and iterating input.groups.fixed.values() instead of input.groups.linked.values(); raise()'s existing per-sibling fixed-group loop at lines 464-478 is NOT modified by this spec -- see non_goals); crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs (plan_version's internal orchestration: TagIndex/NapiTargetsIndex bindings, pre_mutation_checks call with its real six-argument signature, diagnostics merge, CascadeInput construction at line 70); crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs (CascadeInput construction at line 53 gains a `tags` argument via a new `let tags = ws.tags()?;` call; this is not purely mechanical -- plan_snapshot does not call ws.tags() anywhere today, so this introduces a new fallible code path into plan_snapshot's error surface, see AC-014); crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs (GroupTable::resolve, private fn at line 135, gains cross-group conflict detection only -- no dedup, see non_goals). Both real CascadeInput construction sites in production code are covered; no other command constructs CascadeInput.
non_goals: Track 2 (platform-manifest / optionalDependencies writes) — separate track, depends on this one, not addressed here.
Track 9 (cascade_action peer-escalation severity bug, dependency-spec rewrite key bug) — separate, scoped track sharing cascade.rs, sequenced immediately after this one, not part of this spec.

Any change to fixed_group_target's or pre_mutation_checks's own internal logic/signature beyond what's needed to call them from real code — both are already correct for the cases this spec exercises; this track is about wiring, not redesigning them. (Note: unlike pre_mutation_checks, fixed_group_target has no pre-existing dedicated unit test as of this spec — see reasoning. This spec does not add one as a separate task; the real-call-path tests required by AC-002 and AC-004 exercise fixed_group_target indirectly, which is the coverage this spec commits to. Adding an isolated unit test for fixed_group_target directly is out of scope, not because it's undesirable, but because this spec's contract is about the real call path being fixed and tested, not about backfilling unit-test coverage for a helper that was already correct.)
GroupTable::resolve's other existing responsibilities and error paths beyond the new ConflictingGroupMembership detection -- do not refactor unrelated parts of resolve() as a side effect.

Calling pre_mutation_checks from commands/snapshot.rs's plan_snapshot. Reason: plan_snapshot assigns the identical synthetic `0.0.0-<tag>-<sha>` version to every package in the workspace unconditionally (snapshot.rs, `snapshot_versions.insert(pkg.id.clone(), snapshot_ver.clone())` runs for every package regardless of severity or group membership) — there is no divergence between real, distinct release targets for pre_mutation_checks to catch in snapshot mode, since no package ever gets a distinct real target version during a snapshot run. Wiring pre_mutation_checks into snapshot.rs would be a no-op check against synthetic data, not a meaningful protection. This exclusion is a stated design decision (see AC-006), not a silent omission.

fixed_group_target hardcodes callisto_format::SemVerVersioning unconditionally (groups.rs:137), unlike bump_target, which dispatches on base.grammar() including Pep440 (cascade.rs:398-401). This spec's new Fixed-group convergence block calls fixed_group_target as-is; it does not fix this pre-existing SemVer-only limitation. For a Fixed group whose released member's base version parses under VersionGrammar::Pep440, fixed_group_target will still bump it using SemVer parsing/rendering semantics, which may produce an incorrect or unparseable result. This is a known, pre-existing limitation of fixed_group_target itself — not introduced by this spec — and fixing it is explicitly out of scope for Track 1 per the non_goal above (no change to fixed_group_target's internal logic); it belongs to a follow-up track.

raise()'s pre-existing per-sibling fixed-group loop (cascade.rs:464-478), which independently calls bump_target for each sibling when a cascade-triggered severity raise reaches a Fixed-group member via a dependent edge, is left unmodified by this spec. Its output for the target version is superseded within the same solve_cascade fixpoint iteration by the new Fixed-group convergence block, which recomputes and overwrites out.targets for every Fixed-group member from the shared fixed_group_target result after each inner worklist pass completes. This spec does not remove, disable, or refactor raise()'s loop — its severity-assignment side effect (raising a sibling's severity and re-queuing it onto the worklist) remains necessary for the new convergence block to see the raised severity and re-converge; only the loop's independent per-sibling bump_target call becomes redundant, not incorrect-in-isolation for the cases this spec does not test.

GroupCheckOutcome.new_members (the list of a Fixed group's not-yet-released members) is populated by pre_mutation_checks but intentionally not consumed by this spec's plan_version wiring -- only GroupCheckOutcome.diagnostics is merged into VersionPlan.diagnostics. Surfacing new_members (e.g. as a diagnostic or changelog annotation marking a Fixed-group sibling's first release) is a distinct, additive behavior with no basis in REQ-TRACK1-FIXED-GROUP-CASCADE-CORRECTNESS's done_when list and is deferred to a follow-up track. This spec's wiring leaves new_members write-only by design, not by oversight.

Deduplicating a group's own member list when the same PackageId is reachable under two different spellings within one group (e.g. "my-lib" and "cargo:my-lib") is explicitly out of scope for this track. Verified against the live code: fixed_group_target's alignment-base lookup only reads released[0] from a tag-filtered subset, its max_sev computation is idempotent over repeated (id, severity) pairs, pre_mutation_checks's grammar/divergence comparison is idempotent over repeated (id, version) pairs, and solve_cascade's convergence blocks (both the pre-existing Linked-group block and the new Fixed-group block) write out.targets/out.severities through an equality-gated insert into a BTreeSet-backed worklist that naturally collapses a repeated PackageId key -- so an undeduplicated duplicate spelling cannot corrupt AC-001, AC-002, AC-004, or AC-007. Deduplication remains a reasonable follow-up cleanup but is not required for this track's correctness contract.

api_surface.name: CascadeInput.tags
api_surface.description: New field added to the CascadeInput struct (crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs, currently 8 fields: graph, groups, cfg, seed, reasons, named_by, base, pre — none named tags). Required so that the new Fixed-group convergence block in solve_cascade (see the api_surface entry below) can call crate::groups::fixed_group_target(g, input.base, &out.severities, input.tags, input.pre) instead of computing each Fixed-group member's target independently via bump_target. Both real construction sites must supply it: commands/version.rs:70 (plan_version) and commands/snapshot.rs:53 (plan_snapshot). TagIndex is defined in crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs and exposes last_tag(&self, id: &PackageId) -> Option<&LastTag> and an empty() constructor for tests.

api_surface.name: cascade::solve_cascade (new Fixed-group convergence block)
api_surface.signature: Added within solve_cascade's existing `while changed { ... }` fixpoint loop (crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs), as a second per-iteration block positioned after the pre-existing Linked-group block (lines 314-379). No new free function or public signature is introduced; solve_cascade's own signature (`pub fn solve_cascade<D: DependencyResolver>(input: CascadeInput<'_, D>) -> Result<CascadeOutcome, GraphError>`) is unchanged.
api_surface.description: For each `g` in `input.groups.fixed.values()`: collect that group's Package member ids the same way the Linked-group block does (via `g.members(crate::config::GroupMemberKind::Package)` filtered to `GroupMember::Package`). Compute `max_sev` as the maximum of `out.severities.get(id)` over those member ids (defaulting absent entries to `Severity::None`), and for any member whose current severity in `out.severities` is below `max_sev`, raise it to `max_sev` (mirroring the Linked-group block's severity-union step) so severities stay consistent with the shared target about to be computed. If `max_sev > Severity::None`, call `crate::groups::fixed_group_target(g, input.base, &out.severities, input.tags, input.pre)` — the real five-argument signature (`g: &GroupDef, base: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Version>, severities: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Severity>, tags: &TagIndex, _pre: Option<&callisto_format::PreState>`) — exactly once per group per outer-loop iteration, propagating its `Result<Version, GraphError>` with `?`. For every member whose current `out.targets` entry differs from the returned `winner` version, insert `winner` into `out.targets`, set `out.reasons` to `BumpReason::FixedGroupUnion { group: g.name.clone() }`, insert the member id into `worklist`, and set the outer loop's `changed = true` (identical convergence-signaling pattern to the Linked-group block, lines 366-378). This block runs on every seed-triggered pass (AC-001/AC-002's scenario, where both siblings arrive via `input.seed` and are visible in `out.severities` before `raise()` is ever invoked) as well as on any pass where `raise()` has raised a member's severity via a dependent edge, since it re-reads `out.severities` fresh each outer iteration.

api_surface.name: commands::version::plan_version (internal orchestration change; external signature unchanged)
api_surface.description: External signature and return type are unchanged. Internally, plan_version gains: (a) a local `tags` binding capturing the TagIndex currently only produced inline as an unbound argument to aggregate() at line 43 (e.g. `let tags = ws.tags()?;` — `ws.tags()` already returns `Result<&TagIndex, GraphError>`, a borrowed reference, so `tags` is itself `&TagIndex` and must be passed as `tags`, not `&tags`, everywhere it's used, including CascadeInput's new `tags` field); (b) a newly-constructed NapiTargetsIndex, which does not exist anywhere in plan_version today (e.g. `NapiTargetsIndex::load(&ws.config.groups, &ws.root)?`); (c) a call to `crate::groups::pre_mutation_checks(&ws.graph, &ws.config.groups, &base_versions, tags, &napi, &ws.root)` — the real six-argument signature (`_graph: &D, groups: &GroupTable, base: &BTreeMap<PackageId, Version>, tags: &TagIndex, napi: &NapiTargetsIndex, root: &Path`), sourcing `&ws.graph` for `_graph` and `&ws.root` for `root` (Workspace.root is `pub root: PathBuf`, so it must be borrowed, not moved, from a `&Workspace`) in addition to the previously-listed `base_versions`, `ws.config.groups`, `tags`, and `napi` — executed before run_cascade; (d) merging of the returned GroupCheckOutcome.diagnostics into the existing `diagnostics` collection (bound at line 203, passed through escalate() at line 219) so they appear in the final VersionPlan.diagnostics; (e) propagating pre_mutation_checks's Err(GraphError::FixedGroupDivergent | GraphError::GroupGrammarMismatch) as plan_version's own Err result, aborting before run_cascade executes.

api_surface.name: config::groups::GroupTable::resolve
api_surface.signature: pub(crate) fn resolve(raw: &RawGroupTable, index: &IdentityIndex) -> Result<GroupTable, GraphError>
api_surface.description: Signature unchanged. Internal logic gains cross-group conflict detection: while building the fixed_of/linked_of maps (currently populated via unchecked .insert() calls at lines 149 and 180 that silently overwrite an existing entry), if a PackageId being inserted for group G2 already has an entry recorded for a different group G1, resolve() returns Err(GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership { package, groups }) where `package` is the shared resolved PackageId and `groups` lists the conflicting group names (at least G1 and G2), instead of completing the insert and returning Ok. Conflict detection is unified across group kinds: a single resolved PackageId may appear in at most one group total (Fixed or Linked), not one-per-kind. The check compares against a single combined view of both fixed_of and linked_of when performing the insert, not two independently-scoped maps. A duplicate spelling of the same PackageId within one group's own membership list is explicitly out of scope for this track (see non_goals) -- resolve() does not deduplicate it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a Fixed group with two Package members A and B — base_versions = {A: 2.0.0, B: 0.1.0}, tags.last_tag(A) = Some(_) (A has a prior release tag, i.e. A is the 'released' member), tags.last_tag(B) = None (B has never been released) — and a cascade run where both A and B are seeded directly (present in CascadeInput.seed, not reached via a dependent edge raising either package through raise()) with Severity::Minor, both A's and B's computed target version in the resulting CascadeOutcome.targets are the identical value `2.1.0`: the group-aligned version produced by fixed_group_target using alignment base `base[released[0]]` = base[A] = `2.0.0` bumped by the group's max severity (Minor). This is not two independently-bumped versions computed from each sibling's own base version — independent bumping would instead yield A = 2.1.0 and B = 0.2.0, two different targets, which this criterion explicitly rules out.

The behavior in AC-001 is observable through the real, live call path crate::cascade::run_cascade -> solve_cascade -> the new Fixed-group convergence block (added within solve_cascade's `while changed` fixpoint loop, structurally mirroring the pre-existing Linked-group block) -> crate::groups::fixed_group_target, exercised end-to-end by a test that invokes run_cascade (or commands::version::plan_version, which calls it) with both A and B present in CascadeInput.seed — not a test that calls fixed_group_target directly in isolation, and not a test that relies on raise() being triggered by a dependent edge (raise() is never invoked in this scenario, since both siblings arrive via the seed path, not via a cascading dependency edge).

crates/callisto-graph builds and its full test suite (including its integration test binaries) compiles successfully after CascadeInput gains a `tags: &TagIndex` field, with every CascadeInput construction site updated to supply it: commands/version.rs's plan_version (line 70), commands/snapshot.rs's plan_snapshot (line 53), the seven pre-existing CascadeInput literals inside cascade.rs's own #[cfg(test)] mod tests block (lines 698, 779, 850, 947, 1074, 1157, 1237), and the six pre-existing CascadeInput literals inside crates/callisto-graph/tests/cascade_tests.rs (lines 48, 141, 196, 258, 324, 411). None of these thirteen pre-existing test literals construct a Fixed group (they use Linked groups or GroupTable::default()), so all thirteen are updated to supply `tags: &TagIndex::empty()`. `cargo test -p callisto-graph --no-run` (or the workspace equivalent via `just ci` / `moon run :test`) completes with zero compilation errors across all of cascade.rs, its test module, cascade_tests.rs, version.rs, and snapshot.rs.

Given the same Fixed-group two-sibling scenario as AC-001 (base_versions = {A: 2.0.0, B: 0.1.0}, tags.last_tag(A) = Some(_), tags.last_tag(B) = None, both seeded Severity::Minor), invoking crate::cascade::run_cascade directly with a CascadeInput constructed identically in shape to snapshot.rs:53-62 (pre: None, both A and B seeded) returns a CascadeOutcome whose `targets` map holds the identical value `2.1.0` for both A and B. This confirms the fix in solve_cascade's new Fixed-group convergence block applies uniformly regardless of which command constructs the CascadeInput, because commands::version::plan_version and commands::snapshot::plan_snapshot both construct structurally identical CascadeInputs that are passed through the same run_cascade -> solve_cascade path — not because plan_snapshot's own return value exposes this target (it does not; see AC-005, which covers what plan_snapshot actually returns).

Given a workspace with Fixed-group members, running commands::snapshot::plan_snapshot after this fix produces a VersionPlan whose every PlannedBump has `to` equal to the single parsed `0.0.0-<tag>-<sha_short>` version, and a SnapshotReport whose every BumpRecord has `to` equal to that same version — for every package in the workspace, regardless of severity or Fixed-group membership. This fix does not change plan_snapshot's observable return values for any package: the cascade-stage target computed internally by the new Fixed-group convergence block (exercised and asserted directly by AC-004) is computed and then discarded by plan_snapshot's synthetic-versioning step, which unconditionally overwrites every PlannedBump.to and BumpRecord.to with the synthetic snapshot version.

commands::snapshot::plan_snapshot does not call crate::groups::pre_mutation_checks anywhere in its call path -- that wiring is scoped to commands/version.rs's real orchestration only, per this spec's non_goals, with the stated reason that snapshot mode assigns every package an identical synthetic version and so never produces distinct real target versions for pre_mutation_checks's divergence check to evaluate.

Given a Fixed group with two released members whose base_versions are both present in `base` and both parse under the group's grammar, but whose parsed versions are unequal (e.g. member A base_versions=1.0.0, member B base_versions=1.1.0, both with a tag present in `tags`), running the real callisto version command (commands::version::plan_version) returns Err(GraphError::FixedGroupDivergent { group, members }) as its own Err result, and run_cascade never executes. Given instead two released members whose parsed versions use different version grammars -- one a Cargo.toml member (SemVer) and one a pyproject.toml member (Pep440), both tagged -- plan_version returns Err(GraphError::GroupGrammarMismatch { group, members }) under the same no-cascade-execution condition.

Given a workspace where a Fixed group's napi package.json exists at the conventional path (root/<main-package-name>/package.json) but contains invalid JSON (e.g. a truncated or syntactically malformed file), running commands::version::plan_version returns Err(GraphError::Manifest(ManifestError::Parse { path, format: ManifestFormat::PackageJson, .. })) where `path` is that package.json's path, and run_cascade never executes -- no VersionPlan is produced. The same applies, mutatis mutandis, when the file exists but cannot be read (Err(GraphError::Manifest(ManifestError::Read { path, .. }))).

Given a base_versions/TagIndex/NapiTargetsIndex combination for which pre_mutation_checks succeeds and returns a GroupCheckOutcome with one or more non-empty diagnostics, running commands::version::plan_version produces a VersionPlan whose `diagnostics` field contains those same diagnostic entries (in addition to any diagnostics plan_version already produces, e.g. EmptyChangeset), confirming the diagnostics are merged into the real output rather than discarded.

commands::version::plan_version has access to a TagIndex and a NapiTargetsIndex (via NapiTargetsIndex::load or equivalent -- no such construction exists in plan_version prior to this fix) and passes both to pre_mutation_checks (along with `&ws.graph` and `&ws.root`, the two additional real-signature arguments), and passes the TagIndex value to CascadeInput's new `tags` field. The exact binding structure (new local variable vs. inline expression) is an implementation choice, not part of this criterion -- only that all required values are correctly constructed and reach both call sites is required.

Given two Fixed group definitions in a workspace's raw TOML config where a member is spelled differently in each (group A lists "my-lib", group B lists "cargo:my-lib") but both spellings resolve, via the IdentityIndex, to the same real PackageId, GroupTable::resolve returns Err(GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership { package, groups }) where `package` equals that shared resolved PackageId and `groups` contains the names of both A and B.

Given a workspace TOML config where a resolved PackageId is listed as a member of one Fixed group and, under a different spelling, as a member of one Linked group, GroupTable::resolve returns Err(GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership { package, groups }) naming both the Fixed and the Linked group, confirming the conflict check spans both group kinds and is not scoped separately to fixed_of and linked_of.

Given a workspace group config where a single PackageId legitimately belongs to exactly one group (the ordinary, allowed case -- no other group claims the same resolved id), GroupTable::resolve returns Ok(..) for that config and GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership is not constructed anywhere during that resolve() call.

Given a workspace config with no group spelling conflicts (the pre-existing, unmodified test fixtures used by GroupTable::resolve's current test suite), GroupTable::resolve's output is unchanged from its pre-fix behavior -- all existing group-resolution tests pass unmodified after this fix, with no test assertions altered to accommodate the new conflict-detection logic.

The test suite added for this spec includes at least one test per bug that exercises the real call path rather than only the pre-existing helper function in isolation: bug 1 via a test invoking crate::cascade::run_cascade (or a command that calls it, e.g. plan_version or plan_snapshot) with both Fixed-group siblings present in CascadeInput.seed and asserting on run_cascade's output, not merely a direct unit-test call to fixed_group_target and not relying on raise() being triggered; bug 2 via a test invoking commands::version::plan_version and asserting on its Err/diagnostics output, not merely a direct unit-test call to pre_mutation_checks; bug 3 via a test invoking GroupTable::resolve with a full RawGroupTable/IdentityIndex pair reflecting realistic TOML-parsed config, not a synthetic direct construction of internal maps that bypasses resolve()'s own entry point.

Given a workspace where ws.tags() (TagIndex::build) returns Err(_) -- for example because git tag data cannot be read via the workspace's git_access() -- running commands::snapshot::plan_snapshot propagates that same Err as its own Err result, and no VersionPlan or SnapshotReport is produced. A test forces TagIndex::build to fail (e.g. via a CommandRunner stub that errors on the git tag-listing call) and asserts plan_snapshot returns Err rather than panicking or silently proceeding with an empty/partial TagIndex.

revision_note: Corrected after canon-exit-gate retry 1 returned 7 blockers, all addressed: BLK-01 (critical) -- bug 1 was misdiagnosed as a fix to raise()'s per-sibling loop (cascade.rs:464-478), which the exit-gate proved unreachable for AC-001's seed-path scenario (solve_cascade computes seeded targets itself at line 198, before raise() ever runs) and, even when raise() does run, is guarded by `sev > sib_sev` which is false for AC-001's equal-severity siblings. Restructured scope, api_surface (replaced the 'cascade::raise' entry with a new 'cascade::solve_cascade (new Fixed-group convergence block)' entry describing a block mirroring the existing Linked-group block at lines 314-379), and AC-001/AC-002 to target a new Fixed-group convergence block inside solve_cascade's fixpoint loop instead, with AC-001's scenario now explicitly seeded (not raise()-triggered). Added two non_goals documenting that raise()'s existing loop is left unmodified (superseded, not removed) and that fixed_group_target's SemVer-only hardcoding is a known pre-existing gap out of scope for this track (BLK-05's second half). BLK-02 -- AC-004 was unobservable through plan_snapshot (which discards cascade targets); restated AC-004 to assert directly on run_cascade's CascadeOutcome.targets, with justification resting on structurally identical CascadeInput construction rather than a nonexistent observation path. BLK-03 -- AC-010c required an unstated resolve() behavior change forbidden by the original non_goals; added an explicit dedup requirement to the GroupTable::resolve api_surface entry (`.dedup()` after the existing `.sort()` calls at lines 164/195) and carved out an exception in non_goals item 4. BLK-04 -- fixed the fixed_group_target call sketch to the real five-argument signature (g, base, severities, tags, pre) in the new solve_cascade api_surface entry. BLK-05 -- AC-001 now states fully concrete fixture values (base_versions = {A: 2.0.0, B: 0.1.0}, tags.last_tag(A)=Some, tags.last_tag(B)=None, both seeded Minor -> both target 2.1.0) with the alignment-base mechanism (base[released[0]]) stated explicitly; added a non_goal covering the SemVer-only/PEP440 gap in fixed_group_target rather than leaving it ambiguous. BLK-06 -- AC-005 restated against the actual returned VersionPlan.bumps and SnapshotReport.bumps values instead of the unobservable private `snapshot_versions` local, and the unrunnable before/after framing was dropped. BLK-07 -- the plan_version api_surface entry now lists pre_mutation_checks's real six arguments (adding &ws.graph and ws.root) and corrects the tags borrow note (ws.tags() already returns &TagIndex, so `tags` is passed directly, not `&tags`). SECOND AUDIT ROUND (after retry-1 passed then a fresh audit found 4 more issues): the BLK-03 fix described above (adding `.dedup()` to GroupTable::resolve, carving out a non_goals exception) has been RETRACTED. A second audit traced fixed_group_target's released[0]-only alignment-base lookup, its idempotent max_sev computation, pre_mutation_checks's idempotent divergence comparison, and solve_cascade's equality-gated/BTreeSet-backed convergence writes, and confirmed an undeduplicated duplicate spelling cannot corrupt any of AC-001/AC-002/AC-004/AC-007 -- the dedup requirement was not load-bearing and has been removed as scope creep: AC-010c deleted, the GroupTable::resolve api_surface entry's dedup clause removed, non_goals item 4 restored to its unqualified original form, and a new non_goals item added explicitly deferring within-group dedup with the traced justification. Three further issues from that same audit round were also fixed: AC-003 rewritten to additionally cover the six CascadeInput literals in crates/callisto-graph/tests/cascade_tests.rs (lines 48, 141, 196, 258, 324, 411) alongside cascade.rs's own seven test-module literals -- all thirteen confirmed to construct no Fixed groups (only Linked/default), so all can take TagIndex::empty(); a new AC-014 added covering plan_snapshot's newly-introduced ws.tags() fallibility; a new non_goals item added documenting GroupCheckOutcome.new_members as intentionally write-only in this spec's wiring.
reasoning: Read cascade.rs's full solve_cascade, bump_target, and raise() functions plus groups.rs's fixed_group_target and pre_mutation_checks, config/groups.rs's resolve(), and commands/version.rs and commands/snapshot.rs in full before making any edit, per the correction instructions. Confirmed every line number and signature cited in the blocker list against the live source rather than trusting the paraphrase. Key structural decision: rather than inventing a new free function, the Fixed-group fix is expressed as a second block inside solve_cascade's existing `while changed` fixpoint loop, exactly mirroring the pattern already proven correct for Linked groups at lines 314-379 -- this keeps the fix minimal, keeps it participating in the same convergence/worklist machinery, and naturally supersedes raise()'s independent per-sibling bump_target calls without requiring raise() itself to change (since the new block re-reads and overwrites out.targets from the shared fixed_group_target result on every outer-loop pass, regardless of how a member's severity got there). Chose to add explicit non_goals for both the raise()-loop-left-unmodified point and the fixed_group_target SemVer/PEP440 gap rather than silently omitting them, since the correction instructions and this spec's own judgment standard require every known-but-unaddressed gap to be stated rather than glossed. AC-010c's dedup requirement was later retracted in a second audit round after being traced as not load-bearing for any other criterion in this spec -- see revision_note.
